paper_metadata.title: Hybrid Quantum Classical Model for Enhanced Cross Border Financial Fraud Detection

summary: The paper proposes a hybrid quantum–classical fraud detection pipeline comparing a classical SVM with a QSVM using angle-encoded quantum feature maps simulated in PennyLane with PCA-reduced features (≤4 dimensions). Results are presented only qualitatively through ROC and confusion matrix visualizations, with no reported numerical accuracy, F1, or runtime values, so quantitative performance improvements cannot be verified.

experiments.description: Comparative experiment of a classical SVM baseline versus a quantum support vector machine for cross-border financial fraud detection on a preprocessed transaction dataset, using quantum feature encoding and a quantum kernel on a simulator.

algorithm.variant: QSVM with angle encoding and quantum kernel (Z and ZZ feature maps mentioned)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical features are normalized to [0, π] and mapped to qubit rotation angles; entangling CNOT gates are used to capture feature correlations; quantum kernel computed from overlap of encoded states.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary classification of transactions into genuine (0) vs fraud (1) using a quantum kernel SVM.

problem_instance.description: Cross-border financial transaction fraud detection on a tabular dataset with transaction attributes including amount, country risk, time of day, sender blacklisted, and sender age days.

dataset_specification.description: Columns: Transaction ID, Amount, Country Risk, Time of Day, Sender Blacklisted, Sender Age Days, Label. Time of Day encoded Day/Night to 0/1. PCA reduces features to at most 4 components.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Data validation for required columns; categorical Time of Day encoded to numerical 0/1; filtering by Time of Day, Country Risk, Amount, Sender Age Days, Sender Blacklisted; standardization to mean 0 and std 1; PCA to a maximum of four components; features normalized to [0, π] before quantum encoding.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Comparison of classical SVM and QSVM using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, false positive rate, ROC curves, and confusion matrices.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Standardization and PCA; categorical encoding of Time of Day; feature filtering; normalization to [0, π].
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Performance metrics and visualizations including ROC curves and confusion matrices.

speedup_claims.conditions: Comparative study on a preprocessed cross-border financial transaction dataset using simulator-based QSVM with angle encoding and quantum kernel.
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports qualitative claims of competitive performance and improved recall/false-positive trade-offs, but no explicit speedup factor, asymptotic advantage, or runtime comparison is provided.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not specified; the paper does not report qubit counts, circuit depth, kernel evaluation cost, or dataset scaling needed for advantage.
limiting_factors: No runtime comparison with classical SVM
No complexity or scaling analysis for the quantum kernel

notes: Paper explicitly states PennyLane quantum circuit simulation but does not name a specific QPU, so hardware.type inferred as simulator_other.
Number of qubits is not explicitly stated; inferred to depend on the reduced feature dimension (up to 4 PCA components) used for angle encoding, but exact qubit count is not reported.
Circuit depth is not reported; only that the circuit uses angle encoding and entangling CNOT gates.
No asymptotic complexity or speedup order is provided; set to none_proven.
The paper discusses QSVM benefits conceptually but does not present numerical experimental results comparing QSVM vs classical SVM.
Figures (ROC curve, confusion matrix, KPI dashboard) are referenced but no numerical values or dataset scale are provided, preventing advantage evaluation.
